walkthroughs.body_html:
Jean Piaget said children think differently at different ages.

  • 0-2: Sensorimotor — touch, taste, grab.
  • 2-7: Preoperational — pretend play, words.
  • 7-11: Concrete operational — real-world logic.
  • 11+: Formal operational — abstract ideas.

Babies learn through senses and movement.

At about 8 months they realise things still exist when hidden — 'object permanence'. Peek-a-boo time. 👶

By 11+, you can think about ideas that aren't there — fairness, the future, what-ifs.

That's why teen years are full of big questions: 'Why?', 'What if?', 'Is that fair?' 🤔
